I will still do what has worked for me here, not play with big changes. On my 16.1 mu, wheat and maize turn one after the other, so I will use the same 16.1 mu for wheat first and then maize after wheat harvest. I have a well, so I will not let the crop go thirsty at the key time. I do not read books for this. I look at my own field, what I did last year, and what the good growers around me are doing. If I am unsure, I will lean a little heavier on fertilizer rather than let the crop go hungry, because losing yield hurts more than wasting a little fertilizer. For wheat, I will use improved seed, put most fertilizer in early, then chase one time with urea when it starts to stand up strong in spring. I will water about 3 times if the season is normal. For maize, I will use hybrid seed, plant after wheat comes off, give base fertilizer plus one urea chasing, and water about 2 times. I am 65 now and there are only 2 people in the house, so I will keep the work simple: rotary tillage, normal spray program, no fancy trial on part of the land. If the weather is decent, I will aim around 550 kg per mu for wheat and 650 kg per mu for maize.
